ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is Beijing time, marked with times such as 0, 9, and 24; the vertical axis is solar altitude. Curve A rises at 0:00 and falls to the horizon at 9:00; the daylight period is 0—9, so A’s day length is 9 hours. Curve B starts at 9:00 and falls to the horizon at 24:00; the daylight period is 9—24, so B’s day length is 15 hours. Then reason: 9 hours and 15 hours are complementary, indicating that places A and B are located at positions with the same latitude value but in opposite Northern and Southern Hemispheres. This day is the summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere, and the latitude of the direct solar point is δ=23°26′. For two places with the same latitude value but in opposite Northern and Southern Hemispheres, the difference in their noon solar altitudes is 2δ, that is, 2×23°26′=46°52′.
